body.statement: Uniformly over the finite slices \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\) induced by complete arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), use leave-one-cell-out residuals only on \(\mathcal V_n\), while keeping the covariance sum on \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\). The resulting unit-heteroskedastic plug-in estimator satisfies \[\max_{k,k'\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|/(s_ks_{k'})=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2}),\qquad \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat s_k/s_k-1|=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-1}).\] In particular, \(\|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\) while retaining every shared treated-, donor-, and pre-treatment-cell product.
body.justification: The multiplier law is usable only if its entire growing covariance matrix, not only each diagonal entry, is estimable under bounded unit heteroskedasticity.
body.gap: The accessible Choi--Yuan article points to Supplement G.2 but does not substantiate a horizon-uniform covariance theorem; Choi--Kwon--Liao's Feasible CLT displays unitwise residual variance only for a fixed group-average functional, and Ben-Michael--Feller leave staggered heteroskedastic inference as a last-mile task.
body.consumer: This gives the feasible covariance input for one studentized whole-curve critical value in a state-policy panel.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) rate for the feasible score loadings that jointly controls \(\widehat c_{kq}-c_{kq}\) and the leave-one-cell-out unit-variance errors at \(o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\).
obligation.obstruction: The variance-replication assumption controls the number of untreated residual replicates, but no frozen assumption or result controls the imputation component \(\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-q)}-m^0_{it}\) or maps the Choi--Yuan block ratios to the required normalized error of \(\widehat c\). Choi--Yuan's feasible variance corollary is homoskedastic and scalar/group-specific, while Choi--Kwon--Liao's feasible CLT is for a fixed group functional and imposes additional nondegeneracy conditions; neither proves a growing \(K\)-by-\(K\) covariance rate for this leave-one-cell-out construction. Declaring the score-loading rate as an assumption would assume the theorem's substantive crux.
obligation.attempted: Separated the feasible covariance error into its exact score-loading error, proved the sharp deterministic bound \(2r_n^{\mathrm{score}}+(r_n^{\mathrm{score}})^2\), and propagated it through the diagonal square roots and correlation normalization. Checked the primary low-rank feasible-CLT result, which does not provide the missing growing-dimensional rate for the frozen plug-in estimator.
obligation.partial_result:
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\) gives
\(\sigma_{uv}=\sigma_u\).  For \(q=(u,v)\), define
\[
\widehat b_{kq}
=\frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{s_k},
\qquad
a_{kq}=\frac{c_{kq}\sigma_u}{s_k},
\qquad
r_n^{\mathrm{score}}
=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
   (\widehat b_{kq}-a_{kq})^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) makes every
division by \(s_k\) valid.  From the definitions of \(s_k\),
\(\Omega_{kk}\), and \(a_{kq}\),
\[
\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}^2
=\frac{1}{s_k^2}\sum_q c_{kq}^2\sigma_u^2
=\frac{\Omega_{kk}}{s_k^2}=1.
\]
The definitions of \(\widehat\Omega\) and \(\Omega\) similarly give
\[
\frac{\widehat\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
=\sum_q\widehat b_{kq}\widehat b_{k'q},
\qquad
\frac{\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
=\sum_q a_{kq}a_{k'q}.
\]
Adding and subtracting
\(\sum_q\widehat b_{kq}a_{k'q}\) and applying Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}}
&\le
\|\widehat b_k-a_k\|_2\|a_{k'}\|_2
+\|a_k\|_2\|\widehat b_{k'}-a_{k'}\|_2\\
&\quad
+\|\widehat b_k-a_k\|_2
 \|\widehat b_{k'}-a_{k'}\|_2\\
&\le 2r_n^{\mathrm{score}}+(r_n^{\mathrm{score}})^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the first asserted rate follows from the precise missing input
\[
r_n^{\mathrm{score}}
=o_{P_n}\bigl((\log(2K))^{-2}\bigr)
\]
uniformly over the finite slices.  To verify all remaining algebra, put
\[
\delta_n
=\max_{k,k'\in\mathcal K_n}
 \frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}},
\qquad
t_k=\frac{\widehat s_k}{s_k}.
\]
The diagonal case gives \(|t_k^2-1|\le\delta_n\); since \(t_k\ge0\),
\[
|t_k-1|=\frac{|t_k^2-1|}{t_k+1}\le\delta_n.
\]
If \(\delta_n=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\), then uniformly in \(k,k'\),
\(t_kt_{k'}=1+o_{P_n}(1)\).  Since every correlation satisfies
\(|\Sigma_{kk'}|\le1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}-\Sigma_{kk'}|
&\le
\frac{\delta_n}{t_kt_{k'}}
+|\Sigma_{kk'}|
 \left|\frac{1}{t_kt_{k'}}-1\right|\\
&=o_{P_n}\bigl((\log(2K))^{-2}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the claimed covariance, scale, and correlation implications
conditional on the score-loading rate.  The frozen assumptions do not
control the leave-one-cell-out imputation contamination in
\(\widehat e_{it}\), nor do they transport the block perturbation ratios
to \(\widehat c_{kq}-c_{kq}\) in this normalized rowwise
\(\ell_2\) norm.
